Separate neoplastic from non-neoplastic cells

Source: R/neoplastic.R
identifyNonNeoplastic.Rd

Factorises the collapsed arm matrix with NMF, clusters cells on the factor loadings, and treats the cluster with the lowest variance across arms as the non-neoplastic population. Use the returned barcodes as the baseline for identifyCNVClusters() or annotateCNV4B().

Usage

identifyNonNeoplastic(
  inputMatrix,
  estimatedCellularity = 0.8,
  nmfComponents = 5,
  outputHeatmap = TRUE,
  cutHeight = 0.6,
  methodHclust = "ward.D"
)

Arguments

inputMatrix

Collapsed, filtered matrix from filterCells().

estimatedCellularity

Expected tumour cellularity. Works best below about 0.9.

nmfComponents

Number of NMF components.

outputHeatmap

Write a heatmap and violin plot to the output path.

cutHeight

Dendrogram cut height, as a fraction of maximum height.

methodHclust

Linkage method passed to fastcluster::hclust().

Value

A list with cellAssigns (cluster per barcode), normalBarcodes and clusterNormal (the index of the non-neoplastic cluster).

Details

Inspect the heatmap it writes and adjust cutHeight and nmfComponents when the clusters do not separate cleanly.

See also

Other neoplastic classification: estimateCellCycleFraction()

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
nmf_results <- identifyNonNeoplastic(
  scData_collapse, methodHclust = "ward.D", cutHeight = 0.4
)
} # }
